thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SLA breach detected for tenant=PulseGuard on check=embed-availability-prod (alerts firing: 18). Severity: P2. Trace: https://incidents.redwood.ai/2195

alex: I'm on it, grabbing context. Do we know if it's a model-side issue or request surge from tenant?

matt: Looks like a spike in 5xxs from the embed endpoint. Metrics: `embed_requests_total` + `embed_errors_5xx` trending up for PulseGuard only.

monitoring-bot: Query snippet: `sum by (tenant) (rate(embed_errors_5xx[5m])) / sum by (tenant) (rate(embed_requests_total[5m])) > 0.03`

alex: Can someone post the last 10m logs for pulseguard? `kubectl logs -l app=embed-service -n prod --since=10m | grep pulseguard`

sophie: Pasting top error: `ERROR: model-serving timeout after 10s; kv-cache miss; retrying` (retries visible in logs).

priya: That suggests model-side latency causing request timeouts, causing the check to fire. But why only PulseGuard? Their traffic pattern has lots of long prompts.

cs-ops: FYI I already emailed PulseGuard support that we're investigating. They reported intermittent failures starting 04:12 UTC.

alex: For live mitigation: propose temporary paging squelch for the tenant-level SLA check (so engineers can triage without pagers), and set a short-term higher threshold for errors to avoid burners while we open a mitigation. Thoughts? @priya

priya: +1 to squelch. We should keep alerting to a dedicated #pulseguard-ops channel though for a single stream. Also create a one-off dashboard for their recent 1h request latency distribution.

matt: I can create a quick dashboard right now. Will show p50/p95/p99 and 5xx rate per minute. Link coming in 3m.

monitoring-bot: Created ephemeral dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ephemeral/2195-pulseguard. Use `?from=now-1h` to zoom.

alex: Executing mitigation steps:
1) `alertmanager silence add pulseguard-sla --duration=30m --match='tenant=\"PulseGuard\"'` (temporary)
2) route detailed alerts to #pulseguard-ops (no pagers)
3) enable model fallback to smaller quantized variant for PulseGuard traffic (autoswitch)

alex: Running step 1 now.

monitoring-bot: Silence created (id=silence-2195). Ends in 30m. Alerts will still log but won't page.

priya: For step 3, we need a rollout policy change: `routing: if latency>3s -> model=embed-quant-v2` . Who can flip that?

matt: I can flip the temporary routing rule via the runtime console. Doing it now.

matt: Done. Added canary route: tenant=PulseGuard -> embed-quant-v2. Redirecting 100% for next 15m.

sophie: Early telemetry: error rate dropped ~40% after routing change, p95 down from 6.2s to 2.1s. Still seeing occasional 504s though.

alex: Good. While that stabilizes, we need a post-incident plan: adjust the tenant-specific alert thresholds and add a rate-limited suppressor for affinity spikes. Drafting runbook changes: short-term threshold bump, add debounce window, and add a dashboard panel with KV-cache hit-rate per tenant.

priya: Please include steps for Dedicated customers vs Hosted customers — different SLA gates. Also add rollback instructions for the routing override.

cs-ops: I'll prepare the customer-facing summary for PulseGuard: timeline, impact, actions taken, and mitigation. ETA 1h.

alex: Action items assigned:
- matt: create permanent dashboard and add a KV-cache panel + p99 latency (due EOD)
- sophie: runbook PR with routing rollback + silence guidance (due EOD)
- priya: follow up with oncall handoff and add alert suppression rule proposal to monitoring backlog
- cs-ops: customer comms draft (ETA 1h)

priya: Also propose a new alert variant: tenant-sla-critical -> pages if error_rate>5% for 10m OR if errors>200 in 5m, otherwise log. This reduces noise from small tenants that spike.

matt: I'll open a ticket in monitoring board and link the alert rule draft: https://redwood.quip/monitoring/2195-pulseguard-alert-proposal

monitoring-bot: Ticket created: MON-4821 (PulseGuard tenant alert tuning).

alex: Ok I'm handing off to @priya for the next 30m while I finish collecting logs and follow up on model-side traces. Priya, please escalate to infra if the route flip doesn't hold or errors climb back above 5%.

priya: Oncall takeover acknowledged. I'll watch the dashboard and keep the silence in place until we confirm stability or 30m expires. If errors >5% for 3 consecutive 5m windows, I'll re-engage paging.

sophie: Noted — PR link for runbook will be shared in this thread when ready.

cs-ops: Customer comms draft will include recommended client-side retry guidance and a mention of model fallback.

alex: Thanks team. Closing immediate pager; continue monitoring in #pulseguard-ops. Follow-ups tracked in MON-4821 and runbook PR.

incident-bot: Incident note: SLA alert silenced (id=silence-2195). Follow-up tickets: MON-4821, RUN-2195-rb.

priya: Handoff complete. Leaving watch for next 20m. Ping me in thread for updates or escalate to @matt if needed.
